questions.successCriteria: Student can identify that a paragraph should focus on one main topic.

options.feedbackWrong: This paragraph jumps between different topics. Each sentence is about something different.

options.label: B

options.feedbackCorrect: Correct! Paragraph B focuses on one main idea: the importance of learning English.

questions.stem:
Read the following paragraph. Which is the best topic sentence?

'First, it helps you make friends from different countries. Second, you can understand movies and songs in English. Finally, it is useful for traveling to English-speaking countries.'
questions.successCriteria: Student can select a topic sentence that clearly introduces the main idea.
questions.alignmentNote: Question directly assesses topic sentence identification.
questions.stemIntent: Check ability to identify topic sentence.
questions.commonMisconception: Student may choose a detail as topic sentence or an overly broad statement.

options.label: A
options.text: There are many advantages to learning English.
options.feedbackCorrect: Correct! This sentence introduces the main idea that will be explained with details.

options.label: B
options.text: English is spoken by many people.
options.feedbackWrong: This is a fact, but it does not clearly introduce the details that follow about benefits.

options.label: C

options.feedbackWrong: This is a supporting detail, not a topic sentence.

options.label: A
options.feedbackWrong: This statement does not preview the main points the essay will discuss.

options.label: B
options.text: Learning English is important because it helps with communication, career opportunities, and personal growth.
options.feedbackCorrect: Correct! It lists the three main points that will be explained in body paragraphs.

options.label: C
options.feedbackWrong: This is too general and does not preview anything.

Read this body paragraph. Which part is missing?

'Learning English helps with communication. For example, I can talk to people from other countries. In conclusion, learning English has many advantages.'

options.label: A
options.feedbackWrong: The paragraph does have a topic sentence: 'Learning English helps with communication.'

options.label: B
options.feedbackWrong: Evidence is present: 'For example, I can talk to people from other countries.'

options.label: C
options.feedbackCorrect: Correct! The paragraph has a topic sentence and evidence but no explanation of how the evidence supports the topic.

options.label: D
options.feedbackWrong: It has a concluding sentence: 'In conclusion, learning English has many advantages.'

questions.stem:
Which transition word best fills the blank?

'Learning English is useful for school. _______, it can help you get a job.'

options.label: A
options.feedbackWrong: 'However' shows contrast, not addition. The sentence is adding another reason.

options.label: B

questions.stem:
Which conclusion best restates the main points and adds a final thought?

Essay main points: (1) communication, (2) career, (3) personal growth.
questions.successCriteria: Student can evaluate which conclusion effectively summarizes without copying word-for-word.
questions.alignmentNote: Conclusion writing is a key organizational skill.
questions.stemIntent: Check ability to write a proper conclusion.
questions.commonMisconception: Student may think simply repeating the thesis is sufficient.

options.label: A
options.text: This essay talked about communication, career, and growth. In conclusion, learning English is important.
options.feedbackWrong: This simply lists the points and repeats the thesis. It lacks a final thought.

options.label: B
options.text: In conclusion, learning English helps you communicate with more people, improves your career opportunities, and allows you to grow personally. Embracing this skill can open many doors.
options.feedbackCorrect: Correct! It restates the main points in a fresh way and adds a final thought about opening doors.

options.label: C
options.text: Communication, career, personal growth. These are the reasons.
options.feedbackWrong: This is too brief and does not restate ideas fully or add a thoughtful final comment.

questions.stem: Write one body paragraph about how learning English helps with career opportunities. Your paragraph should follow the TEE C format (Topic sentence, Evidence, Explanation, Concluding sentence).
questions.successCriteria: Student produces a coherent paragraph with all four components and appropriate focus.
questions.ossdExpectation: Write in a variety of forms for different purposes and audiences.
questions.alignmentNote: Writing a paragraph is a form of writing assessed under C1.
questions.stemIntent: Check ability to construct a TEE C body paragraph.
questions.commonMisconception: Student may omit explanation or write a weak topic sentence.
questions.rubric: Topic sentence clearly states that learning English improves career opportunities (e.g., 'Learning English can improve your career opportunities in many ways.'). Evidence provides a specific example (e.g., 'For example, many companies require employees to speak English.'). Explanation connects the evidence to the topic (e.g., 'This shows that English skills make you more eligible for international jobs.'). Concluding sentence wraps up (e.g., 'Therefore, learning English is a valuable investment for your future.'). Full paragraph is coherent and on topic.
questions.sampleStrongAnswer: Learning English can greatly improve your career opportunities. For instance, many multinational companies require employees to speak English fluently. This means that by learning English, you become eligible for a wider range of jobs and can work in different countries. In conclusion, English skills open doors to better employment options.

reteachModules.trigger: Student selects Paragraph A (jumping between unrelated topics) on diagnostic Q1.
reteachModules.studentMisunderstanding: Student thinks it is acceptable to include multiple unrelated topics in a single paragraph, not realizing that a paragraph must focus on one main idea for coherence.

miniLesson.explain: A paragraph must focus on one main idea. Use the hamburger analogy: the topic sentence is the top bun (states the main idea), the supporting details are the meat and ingredients (explain the main idea), and the concluding sentence is the bottom bun (wraps up). If you jump between different topics, your reader gets confused. For example, paragraph A: 'Yesterday I went to the store. Then I studied math. My sister likes dogs. I also play soccer.' — this jumps topics and lacks unity. Paragraph B: 'Learning English is important. It helps you communicate with more people and get a better job. Many resources are available online to practice English.' — this stays on one topic: the importance of learning English.
miniLesson.example: Bad (jumping topics): 'Yesterday I went to the store. Then I studied math. My sister likes dogs. I also play soccer.' Good (one main idea): 'Learning English is important. It helps you communicate with more people and get a better job. Many resources are available online to practice English.'
miniLesson.memoryAnchor: One paragraph = one hamburger. Each hamburger has one type of meat (one main idea). Don't mix chicken and beef in the same burger!

guidedPractice.prompt:
Which paragraph focuses on one main topic?

Paragraph A: 'I like pizza. My dog is brown. The weather is sunny.'
Paragraph B: 'Baking a cake requires three steps. First, mix the ingredients. Second, bake the batter. Finally, decorate the cake.'
guidedPractice.answer: Paragraph B focuses on one main topic: baking a cake. Paragraph A jumps from pizza to dog to weather.

guidedPractice.prompt:
Rewrite the following paragraph so that it focuses on one main topic (the benefits of exercise). Remove any sentences that do not belong.

'Exercise is good for your health. It strengthens your heart and lungs. My favorite color is blue. Also, exercise helps you sleep better. Cats are independent pets. In addition, exercise improves your mood.'
guidedPractice.answer: Exercise is good for your health. It strengthens your heart and lungs. Also, exercise helps you sleep better. In addition, exercise improves your mood.

guidedPractice.prompt: Write one paragraph (3-5 sentences) about the importance of saving money. Your paragraph must have a topic sentence, supporting details, and a concluding sentence. Stay on one main idea.
guidedPractice.answer: Saving money is important for financial security. For example, it helps you pay for unexpected expenses like car repairs. Additionally, saving allows you to reach long-term goals like buying a house. In conclusion, saving money provides peace of mind and future opportunities.

reteachModules.trigger: Student selected an incorrect option for identifying a topic sentence.
reteachModules.studentMisunderstanding: Student may omit the topic sentence or write one that does not clearly state the paragraph's main idea, often confusing a supporting detail or a general fact as the topic sentence.

miniLesson.explain: A paragraph is like a hamburger: the topic sentence is the top bun. It tells the reader the main idea of the whole paragraph. Every detail in the paragraph should support that main idea. Without a clear topic sentence, the reader will not know what the paragraph is about.
miniLesson.example: Consider this paragraph: 'First, it helps you make friends from different countries. Second, you can understand movies and songs in English. Finally, it is useful for traveling.' The best topic sentence is: 'There are many advantages to learning English.' This sentence tells the reader the paragraph will list benefits.
miniLesson.memoryAnchor: Remember: TOP bun = TOPic sentence. It sits on top and tells what the whole paragraph is about.

guidedPractice.prompt: Which sentence is the topic sentence? Paragraph: 'Pizza is a popular food. It has cheese, sauce, and toppings. Many people enjoy pizza for dinner.'

Read the paragraph: '________. For example, it can help you get a better job. Also, you can make friends from other countries. Finally, travel becomes easier.' Choose the best topic sentence: A) English is hard. B) Learning English has many benefits. C) I study English every day.
guidedPractice.answer: B) Learning English has many benefits.

guidedPractice.prompt: Write a topic sentence for a paragraph that will explain three reasons why exercise is good for health.

reteachModules.trigger: Student selects a thesis statement that does not preview the main points of the essay in Q3.
reteachModules.studentMisunderstanding: The student thinks a simple statement of the topic is sufficient for a thesis, not realizing that a thesis should also preview the main points that will be explained in the body paragraphs.

miniLesson.explain: A thesis statement is the last sentence of your introduction. It tells the reader your main idea AND previews the key points you will discuss in the body paragraphs. Without a preview, the reader doesn’t know what to expect. For example, a thesis that says 'Learning English has many benefits' is too vague. A better thesis would be 'Learning English is important because it improves communication, career opportunities, and personal growth.' This tells the reader exactly what the essay will cover.
miniLesson.example: From our lesson: 'Learning English is important because it helps with communication, career opportunities, and personal growth.' This thesis states the topic (learning English) and previews three reasons that become body paragraphs.
miniLesson.memoryAnchor: Think of a thesis as a road map. It shows the destination (main idea) and the route (preview of points). Without a map, you might get lost!

guidedPractice.prompt: Which of the following thesis statements previews the main points of the essay? A) 'Dogs are great pets.' B) 'Dogs are great pets because they are loyal, fun, and protective.' Choose A or B and explain why.
guidedPractice.answer: B) 'Dogs are great pets because they are loyal, fun, and protective.' This previews three reasons that will be explained in body paragraphs. A does not preview any points.

guidedPractice.prompt: Rewrite this thesis to include a preview: 'Exercise is beneficial.'
guidedPractice.answer: Exercise is beneficial because it improves physical health, mental well-being, and social connections.

guidedPractice.prompt: Write a thesis statement for an essay about the importance of learning a second language. Your thesis should preview three main points you would discuss in body paragraphs.
guidedPractice.answer: Learning a second language is important because it enhances cognitive skills, opens up career opportunities, and allows you to connect with more people.

reteachModules.trigger: When a student selects the incorrect missing TEE C element in the diagnostic question (chooses topic sentence, evidence, or concluding sentence instead of explanation), they will receive this reteach module.
reteachModules.studentMisunderstanding: The student may think that only a topic sentence and evidence are needed in a body paragraph, not realizing the importance of an explanation that connects evidence back to the topic.

miniLesson.explain: A body paragraph in an essay follows the TEE C format: Topic sentence, Evidence, Explanation, Concluding sentence. The topic sentence states the main idea of the paragraph. Evidence supports that idea with a fact, example, or quote. Explanation explains how the evidence proves the topic sentence. The concluding sentence wraps up the paragraph and transitions to the next idea. Without explanation, the reader does not understand why the evidence matters.
miniLesson.example: Example body paragraph: 'Learning English helps you communicate with more people. (Topic sentence) For example, you can talk to international friends and colleagues. (Evidence) This shows that English breaks language barriers and allows you to connect with a wider community. (Explanation) In conclusion, improving your communication skills through English is valuable. (Concluding sentence)'
miniLesson.memoryAnchor: Remember TEE C: Topic, Evidence, Explanation, Concluding sentence. Think of it as a burger: the topic and concluding sentences are the buns, evidence is the patty, and explanation is the cheese that ties it all together.

guidedPractice.prompt: Read this body paragraph: 'Learning English helps with communication. For example, I can talk to people from other countries. In conclusion, learning English has many advantages.' Which part is missing?

Choose the correct explanation to complete the TEE C paragraph: 'Learning English improves career opportunities. For instance, many companies require English. _______. Therefore, learning English is important for your career.' Options: A. This shows that English skills make you more employable. B. English is a fun language to learn.
Write a body paragraph about how learning English helps with personal growth. Use the TEE C format (Topic sentence, Evidence, Explanation, Concluding sentence).
guidedPractice.answer: Learning English can help you grow personally. For example, you can read books and watch movies in English. This exposes you to new ideas and cultures, expanding your worldview. In conclusion, learning English enriches your personal life.

reteachModules.trigger: You selected an incorrect transition word in the diagnostic question.
reteachModules.studentMisunderstanding: You may not know how to use transition words to connect ideas smoothly. This can make your writing feel choppy and hard to follow.

miniLesson.explain: Transition words are like bridges that connect your ideas. They help the reader understand how your sentences relate to each other. For example, use 'first', 'second', 'third' to list steps, 'because' or 'therefore' to show cause and effect, and 'in conclusion' to end your paragraph. Without transitions, your writing can feel like separate sentences instead of a single, flowing paragraph.
miniLesson.example: Without transition: 'Learning English is useful for school. It can help you get a job.' With transition: 'Learning English is useful for school. Additionally, it can help you get a job.' The word 'additionally' connects the two ideas and shows you are adding another point.
miniLesson.memoryAnchor: Think of transitions as the glue that holds your paragraphs together. They guide your reader from one idea to the next.

guidedPractice.prompt: Which transition word best fills the blank? 'Learning English helps you communicate. _______, it helps you get a better job.' (Choose from: However, Therefore, Additionally)
Read these two sentences. Choose the correct transition word to combine them. 'Learning English is fun. ... it is also useful for travel.' Options: In conclusion, Because, Also.

Write one sentence that includes a transition word to add another idea to this sentence: 'English is important for school.' Your sentence should start with a transition word like 'Additionally' or 'Furthermore'.
guidedPractice.answer: Additionally, English is important for future careers.

reteachModules.trigger: Student selects a conclusion that merely repeats the introduction or thesis without summarizing or adding a final thought.
reteachModules.studentMisunderstanding: Student thinks that the conclusion should simply restate the thesis or introduction word-for-word, rather than summarizing main points in a new way and providing a final thought.

miniLesson.explain: The conclusion is the bottom bun of your essay. It should remind the reader of your main points—restating the thesis in fresh words and summarizing the key ideas—plus add a final thought to leave a lasting impression. Do not copy the introduction exactly.
miniLesson.example: For an essay on learning English with main points communication, career, and personal growth, a good conclusion: 'In conclusion, learning English helps you communicate with more people, improves your career opportunities, and allows you to grow personally. Embracing this skill can open many doors.' This restates main points and adds a final thought.
miniLesson.memoryAnchor: Think of the conclusion as the bottom bun: it holds the hamburger together and leaves a satisfying finish. Don't just repeat the top bun (introduction); summarize the meat and add a final bite!

guidedPractice.prompt:
Read these two conclusions for an essay about learning English. Which one properly restates main points (communication, career, personal growth) and adds a final thought?

Conclusion A: 'In conclusion, learning English is important. Communication, career, and personal growth are the reasons.'

Conclusion B: 'In conclusion, learning English helps you communicate with more people, improves your career opportunities, and allows you to grow personally. This valuable skill can open many doors.'
The following conclusion just repeats the thesis: 'In conclusion, learning English is important.' Rewrite it to summarize main points (communication, career, growth) and add a final thought.
guidedPractice.answer: In conclusion, learning English enables better communication, enhances career prospects, and fosters personal growth. Investing time in learning English is a step toward a brighter future.

guidedPractice.prompt: Write a conclusion for an essay with thesis: 'Learning English is essential for global communication, professional success, and personal development.' Your conclusion should restate the thesis in new words, summarize the main points, and add a final thought.
guidedPractice.answer: To sum up, mastering English opens doors to worldwide communication, boosts career opportunities, and contributes to personal enrichment. As you continue to improve your English, remember that each new word you learn brings you closer to these valuable benefits.

questions.stem:
Read the paragraph below. It contains sentences that do not belong. Rewrite the paragraph so that it focuses only on 'the importance of learning a new language.' Remove any off-topic sentences.

"Learning a new language opens up many opportunities. It allows you to communicate with more people. My sister likes to paint. Also, it can improve your job prospects. Dogs are loyal animals. In addition, learning a language boosts brain function."
questions.rubric: Score 1-4: 1 = no change or adds more off-topic; 2 = removes some but not all off-topic or still has minor off-topic; 3 = removes all off-topic, stays on one main idea with minor flow issues; 4 = removes all off-topic, stays on one main idea, and sentences flow logically. Target: 3 or 4 to pass.

retestCards.passRule: Correct on Q1 AND rubric score on Q2 >= 3.

questions.stem: Read the paragraph. 'For example, reading can improve your vocabulary. Also, it helps you learn about different cultures. Finally, it is a great way to relax.' Which is the best topic sentence?

Here are some details about why teamwork is important: Teamwork allows people to share ideas. It also helps finish projects faster. Teamwork builds trust among members. Write a topic sentence that clearly states the main idea of this paragraph.
questions.rubric: The topic sentence must clearly state that teamwork is important or has benefits, and must refer to the main idea of the details. Acceptable examples: 'Teamwork has many advantages.' or 'Teamwork is important for success.' The sentence must be a complete sentence.

retestCards.passRule: Student must answer Q1 correctly (option B) and write a topic sentence in Q2 that clearly states the main idea of the provided details about teamwork. Minor wording variations are acceptable as long as the main idea is clear.

retestCards.passRule: All questions must be answered correctly.

Write a body paragraph that follows the TEE C format on the topic: 'Why learning English is important for travel.' Your paragraph must include a topic sentence, evidence, explanation, and a concluding sentence.

retestCards.passRule: Student must correctly identify the missing part in the single choice and produce a TEE C paragraph with all four components (topic sentence, evidence, explanation, concluding sentence).

questions.stem: Which transition word best completes the sentence? 'Studying abroad improves your language skills. _______, it helps you understand new cultures.'

Write one sentence that uses a transition word to add another idea to this sentence: 'Reading in English improves vocabulary.' Start your sentence with an appropriate transition word (e.g., Additionally, Furthermore, Also).

retestCards.passRule: Answer the multiple choice correctly (q1_transition_choice) AND write a sentence in q2_transition_write that uses an appropriate transition word for adding an idea, with the transition at the beginning and a complete, relevant idea.

questions.stem: Which of the following conclusions properly restates the thesis in new words, summarizes the main points, and adds a final thought?
options: In conclusion, learning English is very important for many reasons as I said before.
In conclusion, learning English improves your communication skills, career options, and personal growth. Embracing this language can truly transform your life.

questions.stem: Write a conclusion for an essay with the thesis: 'Regular exercise benefits physical health, mental well-being, and social connections.' Your conclusion should restate the thesis in new words, summarize these three main points, and include a final thought.
questions.rubric: Response should: (1) restate the thesis using different wording, (2) summarize the three main points (physical health, mental well-being, social connections), and (3) include a final thought that leaves a lasting impression. Avoid copying the thesis word-for-word.

retestCards.passRule: Answer single-choice correctly (option 2) AND open-ended response includes all three rubric elements: restatement of thesis in new words, summary of three main points, and a final thought.

dashboardFormat.objective: A paragraph has three parts: topic sentence, details, and ending sentence.；The hamburger analogy: topic sentence = top bun, details = meat and ingredients, ending sentence = bottom bun.；A good paragraph focuses on one main topic; jumping between topics is a weakness.

learningGoals.statement: Identify the parts of a paragraph (topic sentence, supporting details, concluding sentence).
Explain how paragraphs are structured to form an essay (introduction, body paragraphs, conclusion).
Organize ideas into a coherent paragraph and essay using appropriate structure and transitions.

diagnosisRules.condition: student selects option that jumps topics on Q1
student selects wrong topic sentence on Q2
student selects thesis without preview on Q3
student selects missing TEE element on Q4
student selects wrong transition word on Q5
student selects conclusion that simply repeats on Q6

nextActions: [err-paragraph-unity] student selects option that jumps topics on Q1: Remember: a paragraph should focus on one main idea. Let's review that.
[err-topic-sentence-missing] student selects wrong topic sentence on Q2: A topic sentence tells the reader the main idea. Let's practice identifying it.
[err-thesis-not-previewing] student selects thesis without preview on Q3: The thesis should preview the main points of your essay. Let's work on that.
[err-tee-c-format] student selects missing TEE element on Q4: Each body paragraph needs a Topic sentence, Evidence, Explanation, and Concluding sentence. Let's review.
[err-transition-missing] student selects wrong transition word on Q5: Transition words help connect your ideas. Let's practice using them.
[err-conclusion-repeat] student selects conclusion that simply repeats on Q6: A conclusion should summarize main points and add a final thought, not just repeat the introduction.

cards.question: Which paragraph is better written?
options: Paragraph A: 'Yesterday I went to the store. Then I studied math. My sister likes dogs. I also play soccer.'
Paragraph B: 'Learning English is important. It helps you communicate with more people and get a better job. Many resources are available online to practice English.'
misconceptions: This paragraph jumps between different topics. Each sentence is about something different.
✓ Correct! Paragraph B focuses on one main idea: the importance of learning English.
cards.successCriteria: Student can identify that a paragraph should focus on one main topic.
cards.alignmentNote: Question directly assesses organization of ideas in a paragraph, matching C2.
cards.commonMisconception: Student may think including many topics is fine.

cards.question:
Read the following paragraph. Which is the best topic sentence?

'First, it helps you make friends from different countries. Second, you can understand movies and songs in English. Finally, it is useful for traveling to English-speaking countries.'
options: There are many advantages to learning English.
English is spoken by many people.
First, it helps you make friends.
cards.diagnosis: Check ability to identify topic sentence.
misconceptions: ✓ Correct! This sentence introduces the main idea that will be explained with details.
This is a fact, but it does not clearly introduce the details that follow about benefits.
This is a supporting detail, not a topic sentence.
cards.successCriteria: Student can select a topic sentence that clearly introduces the main idea.
cards.alignmentNote: Question directly assesses topic sentence identification.
cards.commonMisconception: Student may choose a detail as topic sentence or an overly broad statement.

cards.question: Which thesis statement best previews the main points of an essay about the importance of learning English?
options: Learning English is important because it helps with communication, career opportunities, and personal growth.
misconceptions: This statement does not preview the main points the essay will discuss.
✓ Correct! It lists the three main points that will be explained in body paragraphs.
This is too general and does not preview anything.
cards.successCriteria: Student can distinguish a thesis that previews body paragraphs from one that does not.
cards.alignmentNote: Thesis previewing is part of organizing ideas in an essay.
cards.commonMisconception: Student may think a simple statement of topic is enough.

cards.question:
Read this body paragraph. Which part is missing?

'Learning English helps with communication. For example, I can talk to people from other countries. In conclusion, learning English has many advantages.'
cards.diagnosis: Check ability to identify missing TEE C element.
misconceptions: The paragraph does have a topic sentence: 'Learning English helps with communication.'
Evidence is present: 'For example, I can talk to people from other countries.'
✓ Correct! The paragraph has a topic sentence and evidence but no explanation of how the evidence supports the topic.
It has a concluding sentence: 'In conclusion, learning English has many advantages.'
cards.successCriteria: Student can identify that the paragraph lacks an explanation after the evidence.
cards.alignmentNote: TEE C structure is a specific organizational strategy.
cards.commonMisconception: Student may think only topic sentence and evidence are needed.

cards.question:
Which transition word best fills the blank?

'Learning English is useful for school. _______, it can help you get a job.'
cards.diagnosis: Check knowledge of transition words for adding ideas.
misconceptions: 'However' shows contrast, not addition. The sentence is adding another reason.
'Therefore' shows cause and effect. Here we are adding an idea, not showing a result.
cards.successCriteria: Student can choose an appropriate transition to add a related idea.
cards.alignmentNote: Using transitions is part of coherent organization.
cards.commonMisconception: Student may confuse transitions for cause/effect with adding ideas.

cards.question:
Which conclusion best restates the main points and adds a final thought?

Essay main points: (1) communication, (2) career, (3) personal growth.
options: This essay talked about communication, career, and growth. In conclusion, learning English is important.
In conclusion, learning English helps you communicate with more people, improves your career opportunities, and allows you to grow personally. Embracing this skill can open many doors.
Communication, career, personal growth. These are the reasons.
cards.diagnosis: Check ability to write a proper conclusion.
misconceptions: This simply lists the points and repeats the thesis. It lacks a final thought.
✓ Correct! It restates the main points in a fresh way and adds a final thought about opening doors.
This is too brief and does not restate ideas fully or add a thoughtful final comment.
cards.successCriteria: Student can evaluate which conclusion effectively summarizes without copying word-for-word.
cards.alignmentNote: Conclusion writing is a key organizational skill.
cards.commonMisconception: Student may think simply repeating the thesis is sufficient.

cards.question: Write one body paragraph about how learning English helps with career opportunities. Your paragraph should follow the TEE C format (Topic sentence, Evidence, Explanation, Concluding sentence).
cards.diagnosis: Check ability to construct a TEE C body paragraph.
cards.successCriteria: Student produces a coherent paragraph with all four components and appropriate focus.
cards.ossdExpectation: Write in a variety of forms for different purposes and audiences.
cards.alignmentNote: Writing a paragraph is a form of writing assessed under C1.
cards.commonMisconception: Student may omit explanation or write a weak topic sentence.
